pages.title: What can ‘nothing’ mean?
pages.alt: Evidence, availability, counterfactual value and revisability answer different questions. Appreciation does not make them interchangeable. Recorded absence: What did a functioning channel observe? A recorded absence can be evidence when the channel discriminates between possible states. A no-event record differs from missing data and from a claim that nothing exists. Missing observation: Was a usable record available? The missing-record sentinel supplies no observation likelihood in the declared implementation. Ignoring missingness requires assumptions; other missingness processes can be informative. Counterfactual appreciation: Against which alternative is an outcome valued? An uneventful outcome can acquire value relative to an avoided harm without supplying favorable evidence. The valuation-only control preserves belief updates and predictive losses by construction. Revisable representations: Can a useful distinction be examined and conditionally retained? The finite counterpart tests access, retention and revision; it does not measure realization of emptiness. Non-reification concerns how a representation is held, beyond recording an absence. Symbols: s is latent state, o observation, p prior and q posterior. In the value illustration, r is reference-event probability, c its cost and C_actual the actual cost. Textual traditions remain situated comparisons, not equivalent doctrines; see the atlas and edition notes. Conceptual proposal → finite enabling operations → a separate human research obligation.

pages.title: From mechanisms to bounded claims
pages.alt: Source reconstruction, corrected comparisons and new extensions remain separate. Recall cohort: 5120 independent agent-world units in 5 declared strata. Recall and independent prediction: What does positive selection add beyond exposure and replay dose? Matched exposure and replay dose separate positive selection from learning and independent prediction. Optimism shifts and predictive accuracy differ; effects depend on the world and comparator. Recorded absence and counterfactual value: Is an absent event evidence, missing data or a different valuation? A no-event token can update belief; the missing-record rule supplies no likelihood. Valuing an avoided harm changes assigned value without creating favorable evidence. Native attention and learned-channel transfer: What reaches attention: a learned channel or a posterior readout? Native GNN/pymdp runs distinguish agent and process; transfer bridges remain separate. The source supplies before-only gaze. A favorable attention shift need not improve prediction. Enacted inquiry and effective access: Does chosen activity make a relevant alternative available? Paid activity, effective access and evidence-based retention or revision are distinct operations. Blocked access can incur cost without revision; exact enumeration retains adverse selections. Adaptive scene sampling: Does an access advantage identify an inquiry-specific advantage? Complete query-conditioned GNN channels expose a context-dependent access advantage. Already-open and uniform controls do not establish a further inquiry-specific benefit. Joint scene and encoding inquiry: Can an encoding be learned and used with scene evidence? Spatial and contingency queries test joint inference over the scene and its encoding. Equivalent laws remain unidentified; excluded support stays unavailable; the reference anchor is stipulated. Glyphs unpack the admitted likelihood: s or z is hidden, o observed and q a known query. Dimensions come from executed GNN. The world glyph is one declared stratum; complete models and controls follow. Synthetic model evidence does not establish human gratitude, clinical benefit, contemplative realization or philosophical equivalence.
